disorders.name: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD)
disorders.ep_note: EP role: psychoeducation to school staff (OCD is anxiety, not defiance), advise against inadvertent ritual accommodation, coordinate with CAMHS/ERP specialist, arrange access provisions in exams where rituals impact completion.
disorders.definition: Presence of obsessions (recurrent, intrusive, unwanted thoughts causing anxiety) and/or compulsions (repetitive behaviours or mental acts to reduce anxiety or prevent a feared outcome), that are time-consuming or cause significant impairment.
disorders.alert: School often inadvertently accommodates rituals (allowing extra time for checking, reassurance, toilet trips) — this MAINTAINS OCD. EP must help school understand the ERP model and agree a consistent, non-accommodating response in coordination with the CAMHS therapist.
criteria: Obsessions: recurrent, persistent thoughts/urges/images experienced as intrusive and unwanted; attempts to neutralise with another thought or action
Compulsions: repetitive behaviours or mental acts performed in response to obsession or following rigid rules, aimed at reducing distress or preventing feared outcome
Time-consuming (>1 hour/day) or cause significant distress or functional impairment
cognitive_mechanisms: Inflated responsibility appraisal — overestimating role in causing harm
Thought-action fusion — thinking something is as bad as doing it
Intolerance of uncertainty
Overimportance of intrusive thoughts
Perfectionism
differential: Tic Disorder (complex tics vs compulsions — no obsessional trigger in tics)
risk_factors: Family history of OCD or anxiety

assessment_tools.name: CY-BOCS
assessment_tools.purpose: Children's Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale — separate obsession and compulsion symptom lists and severity rating.
assessment_tools.ep_note: Gold standard OCD severity measure. Administered by trained clinician. Review with CAMHS.

assessment_tools.name: OCI-CV
assessment_tools.purpose: Obsessive Compulsive Inventory — Child Version. Self-report symptom screen.
assessment_tools.ep_note: Useful initial school-based screen; identifies symptom domains.

Ritual Behaviour: Repeated checking of work — cannot move on until 'just right'
Tapping, touching, arranging items in specific patterns
Cannot leave the classroom without checking everything repeatedly
Impact on Learning: Cannot complete work to their own impossible standard
Significant distress when routines or rituals are interrupted
Cannot share equipment with peers (contamination fears)

home_signs: Rituals before bed, meals, leaving the house
Checking locks, switches, ovens repeatedly
Excessive reassurance seeking ('Are you sure nothing bad will happen?')
Family drawn into rituals — must participate or child is very distressed
ep_formulation: Referral: extremely slow work completion, repetitive checking behaviour, visible distress at school
Do not press child to describe obsessions in detail — refer to CAMHS
Psychoeducation: EP session with school staff on OCD model
Agree school response with CAMHS ERP therapist — do NOT accommodate rituals
Exam provisions: extended time where rituals impact completion

interventions.label: Gold Standard
interventions.text: CBT with Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) — most effective treatment for OCD; delivered by CAMHS specialist

interventions.label: Medical
interventions.text: SSRI medication (fluoxetine, sertraline) — combined with ERP for moderate-severe OCD; CAMHS prescribing

interventions.label: School / EP
interventions.text: Do not accommodate compulsions; coordinate school response with CAMHS ERP plan; exam allowances if needed

classroom_strategies: Coordinate response with CAMHS ERP therapist — consistency is critical
Do NOT complete rituals for child, reassure obsessional fears, or give extra time for compulsions (unless CAMHS agree)
Agreed brief script for reassurance requests: 'That sounds like OCD — I know you can manage this'
Extended exam time only if ERP and CAMHS agree it is appropriate
parent_strategies: Family accommodation reduction plan — with CAMHS guidance
Do not provide reassurance to obsessional questions — brief, consistent response
OCD Youth / OCD Ireland resources
CAMHS specialist OCD pathway — do not wait
